scenes.title: Two-photon live imaging at Rochester: sleeping brain channels widen 60% as clear fluid flushes waste
scenes.era: 2013, University of Rochester Center for Translational Neuromedicine imaging suite

layout.description: High-key modern neurobiology imaging suite with a stainless-steel two-photon laser microscope tower positioned beside a dual-panel scientific monitor comparing narrow waking cortical channels on the left with 60-percent-wider sleeping perivascular channels flushing waste on the right.

positions.who: Lead neuroscientist Maiken Nedergaard (mannequin in white lab coat)
positions.where: standing beside the dual comparison monitor pointing at the expanded sleeping fluid channels

positions.who: First author Lulu Xie (mannequin in white lab coat)
positions.where: seated at the two-photon microscope console adjusting the objective dial
positions.facing: facing the microscope stage and live EEG delta trace

positions.where: standing camera-left holding the clearance rate chart

props.name: two-photon laser microscope tower
props.period_detail: precision brushed-aluminum upright optical microscope on an air-floated table
props.physical_behavior: objective lens focuses cleanly while EEG monitor transitions from fast waking waves to slow delta waves

props.name: dual awake-vs-asleep clearance monitor
props.period_detail: split scientific display showing tight waking tissue vs 60% expanded sleeping corridors clearing tracer twice as fast
props.physical_behavior: sleeping panel sweeps dark waste buildup cleanly out along vessel sleeves

props.name: EEG slow-wave strip display
props.period_detail: screen scrolling tall slow delta waves during natural sleep
props.physical_behavior: switches from rapid low-voltage waking lines to tall slow waves

actions.verb_sequence: watches the EEG trace shift into tall slow-wave sleep -> dials the two-photon depth control
traces the 60-percent wider perivascular fluid corridor across the sleeping monitor panel

reactions.reaction: lean closer to the screen in astonishment as sleeping clearance runs at double the waking speed

scenes.wardrobe: Crisp white University of Rochester laboratory coats over collared shirts and dark trousers.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key clinical daylight across the optical table and dual monitors.
scenes.recognition_hook: The moment slow-wave sleep begins on the EEG, microscopic spaces between brain cells widen by 60 percent and clear fluid washes waste away at double speed.

key_visual.description: researchers at the two-photon microscope watch the monitor show brain fluid channels widen sixty percent during slow-wave sleep

scenes.title: Sleepless night desk vs closed daytime drainage

layout.description: Brightly lit 3 a.m. study desk cluttered with empty coffee mugs and a laptop screen.

positions.where: slumped at the desk rubbing temples beside an alarm clock reading 3:15

props.name: desk clock reading 3:15 and three empty mugs
props.period_detail: ceramic coffee mugs beside a glowing laptop
props.physical_behavior: hand pushes a third mug aside while rubbing forehead

actions.verb_sequence: stares at the 3:15 clock -> presses both palms against his forehead

reactions.reaction: slumps forward as skipped slow-wave sleep leaves daytime fog

scenes.wardrobe: Rumpled button-down shirt with rolled sleeves.
scenes.recognition_hook: One all-nighter measurably raises amyloid buildup in human memory hubs by morning.

scenes.title: Norepinephrine drop unlocks astrocytic aquaporin-4 channels

layout.description: Laboratory bench with a large 3D matte-white architectural cross-section model of a cerebral vessel wrapped by star-shaped astrocytic endfeet.

positions.where: demonstrating the hinged vessel-sleeve model on the bench

props.name: hinged 3D perivascular sleeve model
props.period_detail: matte-white physical teaching model showing astrocytic endfeet around an artery
props.physical_behavior: outer ring opens wider by 60 percent to reveal clear flow channels

actions.verb_sequence: slides the physical model lever from 'Awake' to 'Slow-Wave Sleep', widening the channel gap

reactions.reaction: nods as the two-fold clearance bar chart aligns with the model

scenes.recognition_hook: Star-shaped glial cells form water-lined sleeves around arterial vessels to pump rinse fluid through the cortex.

scenes.title: Protecting the early-night slow-wave wash cycle

layout.description: Calm sunlit-morning bedroom where a sleeper wakes refreshed beside a face-down phone left across the room.

positions.where: sitting up energized in crisp white bedding as morning sunlight enters

props.name: bedside analog clock and docked phone across the room
props.period_detail: phone charging far from the bed while clock shows 7:00 after eight uninterrupted hours
props.physical_behavior: blinds lift to flood the room with morning light

actions.verb_sequence: sits up smoothly -> swings feet onto the floor with clear posture

reactions.reaction: stands tall and alert after a full night's biological wash cycle

scenes.recognition_hook: Consistent deep sleep is your brain's active nightly maintenance shift, not wasted time.
